indict.definition: Formally accuse or charge with a serious crime.
indict.vietnamese: truy tố, khởi tố hình sự, buộc tội chính thức
indict.contextSentence: The grand jury voted to indict the executive on three counts of securities fraud.

jurisdiction.definition: The official power to make legal decisions and judgments over an area or domain.
jurisdiction.vietnamese: thẩm quyền tài phán, phạm vi quyền hạn xét xử
jurisdiction.contextSentence: Cross-border cybercrimes frequently fall outside the territorial jurisdiction of national police.

amorphous.definition: Without a clearly defined shape or form; lacking organization or clear structure.
amorphous.vietnamese: vô định hình, không có cấu trúc rõ ràng
amorphous.contextSentence: The startup operated as an amorphous collective before adopting a hierarchical management model.

metamorphosis.definition: A change of the form or nature of a thing or person into a completely different one.
metamorphosis.vietnamese: sự biến thái, sự chuyển hóa/lột xác toàn diện
metamorphosis.contextSentence: The manufacturing company underwent a painful metamorphosis into a pure software enterprise.

anthropomorphic.definition: Attributing human characteristics, emotions, or behaviors to non-human entities.
anthropomorphic.vietnamese: gán đặc tính người, nhân hóa
anthropomorphic.contextSentence: Users frequently form emotional attachments to language models due to seductive anthropomorphic cues.

morphology.definition: The branch of biology or linguistics that deals with the form of living organisms or words.
morphology.vietnamese: hình thái học (sinh học hoặc ngôn ngữ học)
morphology.contextSentence: Understanding inflectional morphology accelerates vocabulary acquisition across Romance languages.

empathy.definition: The ability to understand and share the feelings of another.
empathy.vietnamese: sự thấu cảm, khả năng đặt mình vào vị trí người khác
empathy.contextSentence: High-performing negotiators exhibit cognitive empathy without sacrificing strategic firmness.

apathy.definition: Lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.
apathy.vietnamese: sự thờ ơ, sự vô cảm, lãnh đạm
apathy.contextSentence: Widespread voter apathy poses an existential threat to democratic accountability.

antipathy.definition: A deep-seated feeling of aversion or hostility.
antipathy.vietnamese: ác cảm sâu sắc, sự thù ghét/bất hảo
antipathy.contextSentence: Historical antipathy between the two regulatory bodies stalled the antitrust investigation.

pathology.definition: The scientific study of disease, or any deviation from a normal, healthy, or efficient condition.
pathology.vietnamese: bệnh lý học, sự rối loạn/sai lệch bệnh lý của một hệ thống
pathology.contextSentence: The report diagnosed the company’s organizational pathology: institutional inertia and zero psychological safety.

conducive.definition: Making a certain situation or outcome likely or possible.
conducive.vietnamese: có lợi cho, dẫn đến, tạo điều kiện thuận lợi cho
conducive.contextSentence: Constant Slack notifications are rarely conducive to sustained deep analytical work.

ductile.definition: Able to be drawn out into a thin wire; easily influenced or pliable.
ductile.vietnamese: dễ kéo sợi, có tính dẻo, dễ uốn nắn
ductile.contextSentence: Copper is prized in electrical engineering because it is exceptionally ductile and conductive.

benevolent.definition: Well-meaning and kindly; serving a charitable rather than a profit-making purpose.
benevolent.vietnamese: nhân từ, hảo tâm, thiện chí
benevolent.contextSentence: The foundation operates as a benevolent trust funding open-source scientific infrastructure.

malevolent.definition: Having or showing a wish to do evil to others.
malevolent.vietnamese: ác ý, hiểm độc, có tâm địa xấu xa
malevolent.contextSentence: Autonomous weapons systems raise ethical perils should they fall into malevolent hands.

benign.definition: Gentle, kindly, or not harmful in effect (in medicine: not malignant).
benign.vietnamese: lành tính, dịu dàng, vô hại
benign.contextSentence: The policy change was initially perceived as benign, but it masked severe regressive tax shifts.

malfeasance.definition: Wrongdoing or misconduct, especially by a public official or corporate trustee.
malfeasance.vietnamese: hành vi sai trái, sự lạm quyền làm trái pháp luật của viên chức
malfeasance.contextSentence: The independent auditor uncovered systemic fiscal malfeasance at the highest levels of the board.

provoke.definition: Stimulate or give rise to a reaction or emotion, typically a strong or unwelcome one.
provoke.vietnamese: khiêu khích, châm ngòi, gợi lên phản ứng dữ dội
provoke.contextSentence: The imposition of unilateral tariffs provoked sharp retaliatory measures from trade partners.

equivocate.definition: Use ambiguous language so as to conceal the truth or avoid committing oneself.
equivocate.vietnamese: nói nước đôi, lập lờ đánh lận con đen để né tránh cam kết
equivocate.contextSentence: When pressed on campaign finance discrepancies, the candidate chose to equivocate.

evocative.definition: Bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind.
evocative.vietnamese: gợi cảm xúc, khơi gợi ký ức mạnh mẽ
evocative.contextSentence: The novelist uses evocative prose to reconstruct the industrial gloom of 19th-century Manchester.

introspective.definition: Characterized by examination of one’s own conscious thoughts and feelings.
introspective.vietnamese: nội tâm, có xu hướng tự vấn và suy ngẫm nội tâm
introspective.contextSentence: Great writers maintain an introspective disposition without falling into self-absorbed solipsism.

conspicuous.definition: Standing out so as to be clearly visible; attracting notice or attention.
conspicuous.vietnamese: nổi bật, đập ngay vào mắt, dễ nhận thấy
conspicuous.contextSentence: There was a conspicuous absence of senior engineers at the sudden restructuring townhall.

circumspect.definition: Wary and unwilling to take risks; prudent, careful to consider all circumstances and consequences.
circumspect.vietnamese: thận trọng, dè dặt, nhìn nhận thấu đáo mọi khía cạnh trước khi hành động
circumspect.contextSentence: Diplomats must remain circumspect when addressing disputed maritime boundaries.

prospectus.definition: A printed document that advertises or provides details of a commercial enterprise, school, or financial product to prospective buyers.
prospectus.vietnamese: bản cáo bạch, tài liệu giới thiệu chi tiết dự án đầu tư
prospectus.contextSentence: Institutional investors scrutinized the IPO prospectus to identify governance vulnerabilities.

homogeneous.definition: Of the same kind; alike, consisting of parts all of the same kind.
homogeneous.vietnamese: đồng nhất, thuần nhất, gồm các thành phần cùng một loại
homogeneous.contextSentence: A culturally homogeneous team frequently succumbs to blind spots and intellectual groupthink.

engender.definition: Cause or give rise to a feeling, situation, or condition.
engender.vietnamese: làm nảy sinh, gây ra, tạo ra (cảm xúc hoặc tình thế)
engender.contextSentence: Opaque compensation matrices invariably engender resentment among top contributors.

indigenous.definition: Originating or occurring naturally in a particular place; native.
indigenous.vietnamese: bản địa, sinh ra và phát triển tự nhiên tại một vùng
indigenous.contextSentence: The ecosystem depends upon preserving indigenous flora against aggressive invasive shrubs.

progeny.definition: A descendant or the descendants of a person, animal, or plant; offspring.
progeny.vietnamese: hậu duệ, con cháu, sản phẩm kế thừa
progeny.contextSentence: Modern generative transformers are the direct intellectual progeny of 1980s neural network theory.

protracted.definition: Lasting for a long time or longer than expected or usual.
protracted.vietnamese: kéo dài dai dẳng, bị giằng co lâu ngày
protracted.contextSentence: After a protracted patent dispute lasting four years, both corporations signed a cross-license pact.

intractable.definition: Hard to control, manage, or deal with; stubborn or unyielding.
intractable.vietnamese: khó giải quyết, nan giải, ngoan cố, bất trị
intractable.contextSentence: The algorithm resolves what was previously considered an intractable computational complexity problem.

detract.definition: Diminish the worth, value, or quality of an achievement, person, or object.
detract.vietnamese: làm giảm giá trị, làm lu mờ, chê bai
detract.contextSentence: Minor typesetting flaws should not detract from the monumental scope of the author’s research.

fidelity.definition: Faithfulness to a person, cause, or belief; or the degree of exactness with which something is copied or reproduced.
fidelity.vietnamese: sự trung thành, lòng chung thủy; độ trung thực (của bản dịch, bản sao, âm thanh)
fidelity.contextSentence: The translator aimed for fidelity to the poet's rhythm as much as to his literal meaning.

incredulous.definition: Unwilling or unable to believe something; showing disbelief.
incredulous.vietnamese: hoài nghi, không thể tin nổi, tỏ vẻ ngờ vực
incredulous.contextSentence: The villagers listened with incredulous faces as the engineer explained that the river would be diverted around their valley.

eloquent.definition: Fluent, expressive, and persuasive in speaking or writing; clearly expressing a feeling.
eloquent.vietnamese: hùng hồn, có tài hùng biện, diễn đạt lưu loát và thuyết phục
eloquent.contextSentence: Her eloquent tribute at the memorial service moved even strangers to tears.

loquacious.definition: Tending to talk a great deal; very talkative.
loquacious.vietnamese: nói nhiều, lắm lời, ba hoa
loquacious.contextSentence: Our loquacious taxi driver narrated the history of every bridge we crossed on the way to the airport.

subvert.definition: Undermine the power, authority, or principles of an established system or institution; overturn conventions from within.
subvert.vietnamese: lật đổ, phá hoại ngầm, làm đảo lộn từ bên trong
subvert.contextSentence: The novel subverts the conventions of the detective story by revealing the culprit on the very first page.

inadvertent.definition: Not resulting from deliberate intention or planning; unintentional, often through lack of attention.
inadvertent.vietnamese: vô ý, sơ suất, không cố ý
inadvertent.contextSentence: An inadvertent click on reply-all sent the confidential salary list to the entire department.

impending.definition: (Of an event, typically an unpleasant one) about to happen; imminent.
impending.vietnamese: sắp xảy ra, đang treo lơ lửng trước mắt
impending.contextSentence: Dark clouds massing over the bay warned the fishermen of the impending storm.

compendium.definition: A collection of concise but detailed information about a particular subject, especially in a single book.
compendium.vietnamese: bản tóm lược toàn diện, sách tổng hợp, tuyển tập
compendium.contextSentence: Her grandmother's handwritten compendium of herbal remedies covered everything from fevers to insect bites.

proscribe.definition: Forbid something, especially by law; denounce or condemn officially.
proscribe.vietnamese: cấm đoán (bằng luật), lên án chính thức, đặt ra ngoài vòng pháp luật
proscribe.contextSentence: The new regulations proscribe the sale of wild-caught songbirds in city markets.

circumscribe.definition: Restrict something within limits; in geometry, draw a figure around another so that it touches it at points without cutting it.
circumscribe.vietnamese: giới hạn, khoanh vùng hạn chế; (hình học) vẽ ngoại tiếp
circumscribe.contextSentence: Her freedom to work was tightly circumscribed by the terms of her student visa.

gregarious.definition: Fond of company; sociable. (Of animals) living in flocks or herds.
gregarious.vietnamese: thích giao du, hòa đồng; (động vật) sống theo bầy đàn
gregarious.contextSentence: Gregarious by nature, he knew the name of every stallholder in the night market within a month of arriving.

egregious.vietnamese: tồi tệ quá mức, trắng trợn, sai lầm rành rành
egregious.contextSentence: Publishing the wrong set of exam results was an egregious error that cost the board its credibility.

susceptible.definition: Likely to be influenced, harmed, or affected by a particular thing.
susceptible.vietnamese: dễ bị ảnh hưởng, dễ mắc phải, nhạy cảm với
susceptible.contextSentence: Young rice seedlings are highly susceptible to cold snaps in early spring.

incipient.root: cip (Latin capere: to take, via incipere: to begin)
incipient.definition: In an initial stage; beginning to happen or develop.
incipient.vietnamese: chớm nở, mới manh nha, ở giai đoạn ban đầu
incipient.contextSentence: Experienced teachers can often spot incipient reading difficulties long before any formal diagnosis.

intermittent.root: mitt (Latin mittere: to send, let go)
intermittent.definition: Occurring at irregular intervals; not continuous or steady.
intermittent.vietnamese: lúc có lúc không, gián đoạn, không liên tục
intermittent.contextSentence: Intermittent showers throughout the afternoon kept interrupting the village football final.

emissary.definition: A person sent on a special mission, usually as a diplomatic representative.
emissary.vietnamese: phái viên, sứ giả, người được cử đi làm nhiệm vụ đặc biệt
emissary.contextSentence: The king sent a trusted emissary across the mountains to negotiate the release of the captured merchants.

tenacious.definition: Holding firmly to something; persistent and determined, not easily giving up.
tenacious.vietnamese: bền bỉ, kiên trì, bám riết không buông
tenacious.contextSentence: A tenacious local reporter spent six years tracing where the flood relief money had actually gone.

inconsequential.vietnamese: không đáng kể, vụn vặt, chẳng quan trọng
inconsequential.contextSentence: What seemed an inconsequential remark at dinner turned out to be the first hint of his resignation.

obsequious.definition: Excessively eager to please or obey; servile.
obsequious.vietnamese: khúm núm, xu nịnh, quỵ lụy
obsequious.contextSentence: The waiter's obsequious bowing cooled noticeably once he learned we were not the mayor's guests.

pseudonym.definition: A fictitious name, especially one used by an author instead of their real name.

healthy.definition: Strong and well; good for your body.
healthy.contextSentence: Eating fruit and vegetables is good for a healthy life.

exercise.definition: Physical activity that keeps your body strong.

manager.definition: Person who is in charge of a shop or a team.
manager.contextSentence: My manager says we can finish work early on Friday.

meeting.definition: Time when people come together to talk about something.
meeting.contextSentence: We have a meeting at ten o'clock in the small room.

salary.definition: Money you get every month from your job.
salary.contextSentence: Her salary is not high, but she likes her job.

nervous.definition: Worried and a little afraid about something.
nervous.contextSentence: I felt nervous before my first day at school.

excited.definition: Very happy about something good that will happen.

lonely.definition: Sad because you have no friends near you.

opinion.definition: What you think about something or someone.

prefer.definition: Like one thing more than another.

boring.definition: Not interesting; making you feel tired.
boring.contextSentence: The book was boring, so I stopped reading it.

the weather.definition: Sun, rain, wind and temperature outside at a time.
the weather.contextSentence: The weather was bad, so we stayed at home.

improve.definition: Become better, or make something better.
improve.vietnamese: cải thiện, làm cho tốt hơn
improve.contextSentence: I want to improve my English before I travel abroad.

experience.definition: Knowledge or skill from doing something, or something that happens to you.
experience.contextSentence: She has two years of experience working in a hotel.

advantage.definition: Something good that helps you do better than others.
advantage.contextSentence: Speaking two languages is a big advantage when you look for a job.

decision.definition: A choice you make after thinking about it.
decision.contextSentence: It was a difficult decision, but we decided to move to the city.

damage.definition: Harm done to something so that it is broken or less useful.
damage.contextSentence: The storm caused a lot of damage to the old bridge.

support.definition: Help or encourage someone, or agree with an idea.
support.contextSentence: My family always supports me when I have problems.

effort.definition: The physical or mental energy you use to do something.
effort.contextSentence: She made a big effort to learn the names of all her students.

recommend.definition: Tell someone that something is good or that they should do it.
recommend.contextSentence: Can you recommend a good restaurant near the station?

reduce.definition: Make something smaller or less in size, amount or price.
reduce.contextSentence: We need to reduce the amount of rubbish we throw away.

society.definition: All the people living in a country or area, with their laws and customs.
society.contextSentence: Young people play an important part in modern society.

protect.definition: Keep someone or something safe from harm or damage.
protect.contextSentence: Parents try to protect their children from danger.

mitigate.definition: Make less severe, serious, or painful.
mitigate.vietnamese: giảm nhẹ, xoa dịu tác động xấu
mitigate.contextSentence: Diversifying investments across uncorrelated asset classes helps mitigate catastrophic portfolio drawdowns.

feasible.definition: Possible to do easily or conveniently; workable and practically viable.
feasible.vietnamese: khả thi, có thể thực hiện được trong thực tế
feasible.contextSentence: Due to severe silicon supply bottlenecks, delivering the product within two months is no longer feasible.

intrinsic.definition: Belonging naturally; essential, inherent to the core nature of a thing.
intrinsic.vietnamese: thuộc về bản chất, nội tại, cố hữu
intrinsic.contextSentence: Curiosity and mastery provide intrinsic motivation that far outlasts short-term monetary bonuses.

versatile.definition: Able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities.
versatile.vietnamese: đa năng, linh hoạt, thích ứng với nhiều mục đích
versatile.contextSentence: Python has established itself as an extraordinarily versatile programming language across data science and web development.

preliminary.definition: Denoting an action or event preceding or done in preparation for something fuller or more important.
preliminary.vietnamese: sơ bộ, bước đầu, mở đầu
preliminary.contextSentence: Preliminary clinical trials indicate that the compound reduces arterial inflammation by thirty percent.

substantiate.definition: Provide evidence to support or prove the truth of a claim or thesis.
substantiate.vietnamese: chứng minh, cung cấp chứng cứ xác thực cho luận điểm
substantiate.contextSentence: The plaintiff failed to produce documentary logs to substantiate allegations of intellectual property theft.

ubiquitous.definition: Present, appearing, or found everywhere simultaneously.
ubiquitous.vietnamese: phổ biến khắp nơi, đâu đâu cũng thấy
ubiquitous.contextSentence: Smartphones have become so ubiquitous that disconnected solitude is now considered an elite luxury.

contentious.definition: Causing or likely to cause an argument; controversial; involving heated legal or political dispute.
contentious.vietnamese: gây tranh cãi gay gắt, dễ châm ngòi bất đồng
contentious.contextSentence: Zoning reform remains the most contentious item on the municipal council’s legislative agenda.

scrutinize.definition: Examine or inspect closely and thoroughly with critical attention.
scrutinize.vietnamese: xem xét kỹ lưỡng, săm soi, kiểm tra gắt gao
scrutinize.contextSentence: Financial regulators began to scrutinize the shadow banking firm’s off-balance-sheet special purpose vehicles.

delineate.definition: Describe, portray, or outline with precision; set forth boundaries clearly.
delineate.vietnamese: phác thảo chi tiết, vạch rõ ranh giới/đặc điểm cụ thể
delineate.contextSentence: The architectural contract must clearly delineate the respective liabilities of the general contractor and structural engineers.

propensity.definition: An inclination or natural tendency to behave in a particular way.
propensity.vietnamese: thiên hướng, xu hướng tự nhiên nghiêng về một hành vi
propensity.contextSentence: Overconfident traders demonstrate a dangerous propensity to double down on losing positions.

discrepancy.definition: A lack of compatibility or similarity between two or more facts or datasets.
discrepancy.vietnamese: sự sai khác, sự không khớp giữa hai số liệu hoặc lời khai
discrepancy.contextSentence: Auditors flagged a five-million-dollar discrepancy between invoice records and warehouse inventory counts.

poignant.definition: Evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret; deeply touching and sharp in impact.
poignant.vietnamese: chua xót, thấm thía, làm thắt lòng
poignant.contextSentence: The documentary delivers a poignant portrait of how deindustrialization hollowed out rural communities.

volatile.definition: Liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse.
volatile.vietnamese: biến động dữ dội, không ổn định, dễ bốc hơi/bùng nổ
volatile.contextSentence: Emerging tech stocks experienced an extraordinarily volatile quarter amid geopolitical semiconductor restrictions.

unprecedented.definition: Never done or known before; completely without prior parallel.
unprecedented.vietnamese: chưa từng có tiền lệ, vô tiền khoáng hậu
unprecedented.contextSentence: The rapid pace of global urbanization has created an unprecedented strain on fresh water reservoirs.

disenfranchise.definition: Deprive someone of the right to vote, or of a right or privilege in society.
disenfranchise.vietnamese: tước quyền công dân/quyền bầu cử, đẩy ra rìa xã hội
disenfranchise.contextSentence: Strict voter identification hurdles disproportionately disenfranchise low-income and transient citizens.

corroborate.definition: Confirm or give support to a statement, theory, or finding with supplemental evidence.
corroborate.vietnamese: chứng thực, củng cố thêm bằng chứng xác đáng
corroborate.contextSentence: Independent seismologists examined telemetry feeds to corroborate the government’s nuclear test claims.

obviate.definition: Remove a need or difficulty; prevent or make unnecessary through proactive design or foresight.
obviate.vietnamese: loại bỏ sự cần thiết của điều gì, ngăn ngừa trước
obviate.contextSentence: Adopting cryptographic zero-knowledge proofs obviates the hazardous practice of transmitting cleartext passwords.

trenchant.definition: Vigorous or incisive in expression or style; keenly perceptive, sharp, and cutting.
trenchant.vietnamese: sắc bén, đanh thép, sâu cay thấu đáo
trenchant.contextSentence: The editorial offered a trenchant dissection of how subsidies entrench fossil fuel cartels.

surreptitious.definition: Kept secret, especially because it would not be approved of; stealthy and covert.
surreptitious.vietnamese: lén lút, vụng trộm, giấu giếm gian xảo
surreptitious.contextSentence: The spyware conducted surreptitious screen recordings and exfiltrated encryption keys to remote servers.

pernicious.definition: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual, subtle, or treacherous way.
pernicious.vietnamese: nguy hại ngấm ngầm, độc hại ăn sâu dần theo thời gian
pernicious.contextSentence: Cynicism is the most pernicious force in democratic institutions because it paralyzes civic participation before reforms begin.

ephemeral.definition: Lasting for a very short time; transient, fleeting.
ephemeral.vietnamese: phù du, chóng tàn, tồn tại trong chốc lát
ephemeral.contextSentence: Viral social media fame is notoriously ephemeral, fading as soon as algorithms reweight user attention.

disparate.definition: Essentially different in kind; not allowing comparison; completely distinct.
disparate.vietnamese: khác biệt hoàn toàn về bản chất, không cùng hệ quy chiếu
disparate.contextSentence: The synthesis paper unified disparate theories from condensed matter physics and algorithmic information theory.

juxtapose.definition: Place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.
juxtapose.vietnamese: đặt cạnh nhau để đối chiếu, làm bật lên sự tương phản
juxtapose.contextSentence: The photographer chose to juxtapose glittering luxury penthouses directly against sprawling riverside shantytowns.

fastidious.definition: Very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail; very hard to please.
fastidious.vietnamese: kỹ tính đến mức khắt khe, cầu toàn đến từng chi tiết
fastidious.contextSentence: Her fastidious attention to typographical kerning and whitespace elevated the design system above its competitors.

esoteric.definition: Intended for or likely to be understood by only a small number of people with specialized knowledge or interest.
esoteric.vietnamese: uyên thâm, mang tính chuyên biệt nội bộ, ít ai hiểu thấu
esoteric.contextSentence: Category theory was once dismissed as esoteric mathematical fluff before finding foundational application in functional programming.

acquiesce.definition: Accept something reluctantly but without protest; submit passively.
acquiesce.vietnamese: bằng lòng ngầm, miễn cưỡng chấp thuận không phản đối
acquiesce.contextSentence: Under intense board pressure, the founder chose to acquiesce to the hostile terms of the venture debt syndicate.

salient.definition: Most notable or important; prominently standing out from the background.
salient.vietnamese: nổi bật nhất, trọng yếu, đáng chú ý nhất
salient.contextSentence: The executive summary distilled the four hundred-page environmental audit down to its three most salient vulnerabilities.

equanimity.definition: Mental calmness, composure, and evenness of temper, especially in a difficult situation.
equanimity.vietnamese: sự bình thản, tĩnh tâm thanh thản đối diện nghịch cảnh
equanimity.contextSentence: The senior flight captain handled the dual engine failure with chilling equanimity, guiding the aircraft to safety.

inexorable.definition: Impossible to stop or prevent; unrelenting and impervious to plea or persuasion.
inexorable.vietnamese: không thể lay chuyển, không thể dừng lại, tất yếu
inexorable.contextSentence: The inexorable demographic aging of the population presents structural insolvency perils for unfunded pensions.

tenuous.definition: Very weak or slight; lacking a sound basis (of a link, argument, or hold on something).
tenuous.vietnamese: mong manh, lỏng lẻo, thiếu cơ sở vững chắc
tenuous.contextSentence: The prosecution's case rested on a tenuous link between the defendant and a phone found near the scene.

cogent.definition: (Of an argument or case) clear, logical, and convincing.
cogent.vietnamese: chặt chẽ và thuyết phục, có sức nặng về lập luận
cogent.contextSentence: Her cogent case for rent control won over even the doubters on the housing committee.

tacit.definition: Understood or implied without being directly stated.
tacit.vietnamese: ngầm hiểu, mặc nhiên, không nói ra thành lời
tacit.contextSentence: By saying nothing at the meeting, the minister gave tacit approval to the cuts.

ambivalent.definition: Having mixed or contradictory feelings about something or someone.
ambivalent.vietnamese: có cảm xúc lẫn lộn, phân vân giữa hai thái độ trái ngược
ambivalent.contextSentence: Many villagers are ambivalent about the new dam: it brings electricity but floods their ancestral farmland.

exacerbate.definition: Make a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling worse.
exacerbate.vietnamese: làm trầm trọng thêm, khiến tình hình xấu đi
exacerbate.contextSentence: Clearing mangroves for shrimp farms has exacerbated coastal erosion across the delta.

untenable.definition: (Of a position, theory, or situation) not able to be maintained or defended against attack or objection.
untenable.vietnamese: không thể đứng vững, không thể bảo vệ hay duy trì được
untenable.contextSentence: Once the leaked emails surfaced, the chairman's position became untenable and he resigned within a week.

specious.definition: Superficially plausible but actually wrong or misleading.
specious.vietnamese: nghe có vẻ hợp lý nhưng thực chất sai lệch, đúng ở bề ngoài
specious.contextSentence: The advertisement relied on the specious reasoning that anything natural must be safe.

perfunctory.definition: Carried out with minimal effort or reflection, merely as a routine duty.
perfunctory.vietnamese: làm cho có, qua loa đại khái, chiếu lệ
perfunctory.contextSentence: After a perfunctory glance at my passport, the border guard waved me through.

ostensible.definition: Stated or appearing to be true, but not necessarily so.
ostensible.vietnamese: bề ngoài, trên danh nghĩa, được viện dẫn công khai (nhưng chưa chắc là thật)
ostensible.contextSentence: The ostensible purpose of the trip was trade talks, but the delegation spent most of its time on the golf course.

belie.definition: Fail to give a true impression of something; or show something to be false.
belie.vietnamese: che giấu bản chất thật, tạo ấn tượng sai lệch; chứng tỏ điều gì là sai
belie.contextSentence: His gentle, soft-spoken manner belies a ruthless instinct for negotiation.

eschew.definition: Deliberately avoid using or doing something, often on principle.
eschew.vietnamese: cố tình tránh xa, kiêng dùng (vì nguyên tắc)
eschew.contextSentence: The poet eschews rhyme altogether, preferring the loose rhythms of everyday speech.

preclude.definition: Prevent something from happening or make it impossible; rule out in advance.
preclude.vietnamese: ngăn trước, loại trừ khả năng, khiến điều gì không thể xảy ra
preclude.contextSentence: A teenage conviction for shoplifting does not necessarily preclude someone from serving on a school board.

gainsay.definition: Deny or contradict a fact or statement; speak against (usually used with a negative).
gainsay.vietnamese: phủ nhận, bác bỏ, cãi lại (thường dùng ở dạng phủ định)
gainsay.contextSentence: There is no gainsaying the courage of the volunteers who stayed behind during the floods.

recalcitrant.definition: Stubbornly uncooperative toward authority, control, or discipline.
recalcitrant.vietnamese: ngoan cố, cứng đầu, bất hợp tác với cấp trên hay quy định
recalcitrant.contextSentence: The teacher's patience eventually won over even the most recalcitrant pupils in the class.

sanguine.definition: Optimistic or positive, especially in an apparently bad or difficult situation.
sanguine.vietnamese: lạc quan, tin tưởng (kể cả khi tình hình không mấy sáng sủa)
sanguine.contextSentence: The coach remained sanguine about the team's chances despite losing their top scorer to injury.

quixotic.definition: Exceedingly idealistic; unrealistic and impractical in the pursuit of noble aims.
quixotic.vietnamese: viển vông, lý tưởng hóa thái quá, kiểu Đôn Ki-hô-tê
quixotic.contextSentence: His quixotic campaign to ban cars from the old quarter attracted admiration but very few votes.

desultory.definition: Lacking a plan, purpose, or enthusiasm; passing aimlessly from one thing to another.
desultory.vietnamese: rời rạc, tản mạn, thiếu mục đích và nhiệt tình
desultory.contextSentence: After a few desultory attempts at conversation, the two strangers on the night bus lapsed into silence.

laconic.definition: Using very few words; concise to the point of seeming blunt or mysterious.
laconic.vietnamese: kiệm lời, ngắn gọn súc tích
laconic.contextSentence: Famously laconic, the old fisherman answered every question about the storm with a shrug and a single word.

obdurate.definition: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action.
obdurate.vietnamese: cố chấp, sắt đá, không chịu lay chuyển
obdurate.contextSentence: Despite weeks of protests, the council remained obdurate and refused to reopen the public library.

mercurial.definition: Subject to sudden or unpredictable changes of mood or mind.
mercurial.vietnamese: thất thường, sớm nắng chiều mưa, tính khí khó đoán
mercurial.contextSentence: The orchestra admired the mercurial conductor's brilliance but dreaded his sudden outbursts at rehearsal.

get up.definition: Leave your bed after you wake up.
get up.contextSentence: I get up at six o'clock every morning.

take off.definition: Remove clothes; or leave the ground, like a plane.
take off.contextSentence: Please take off your shoes before you come in.

look for.definition: Try to find something or someone.
look for.contextSentence: I am looking for my keys, but I cannot find them.

turn on.definition: Make a light or machine start to work.
turn on.contextSentence: It is dark, so please turn on the light.

come back.definition: Return to a place where you were before.
come back.contextSentence: My sister comes back from work at six.

give up.definition: Stop trying to do something; stop a habit.
give up.contextSentence: The test was hard, but I did not give up.

put on.definition: Wear clothes; place something on your body.
put on.contextSentence: It is cold outside, so put on your coat.

find out.definition: Learn a fact that you did not know before.
find out.vietnamese: tìm ra, phát hiện, biết được
find out.contextSentence: I want to find out what time the shop opens.

carry out.definition: Do or complete a piece of work, a plan or a test.
carry out.contextSentence: The team will carry out a survey of local shops next week.

work out.definition: Find the answer to a problem, or finish well in the end.
work out.contextSentence: I cannot work out how to use this washing machine.

set up.definition: Start a business or organise something so that it is ready.
set up.contextSentence: They set up a small shop in the town centre last year.

put off.definition: Decide to do something later than planned.
put off.contextSentence: We had to put off the picnic because of the rain.

turn down.definition: Say no to an offer or an invitation, or make a sound quieter.
turn down.contextSentence: She turned down the job because the salary was too low.

break down.definition: Stop working because of a fault, or fail to continue.
break down.contextSentence: Our car broke down on the way to the airport.

look after.definition: Take care of a person, an animal or a thing.
look after.contextSentence: Could you look after my cat while I am on holiday?

bring up.definition: Raise a child, or start talking about a subject.
bring up.contextSentence: My grandparents brought up five children on a small farm.

scale up.definition: Increase the size, amount, or production capacity of something according to a fixed ratio or expanding demand.
scale up.vietnamese: mở rộng quy mô, nâng công suất vận hành
scale up.contextSentence: The biotech venture secured forty million dollars to scale up bioreactor production for clinical distribution.

wind up.definition: Bring an activity to an end, settle affairs; or find oneself in an unexpected situation or place.
wind up.vietnamese: kết thúc, thanh lý giải thể (doanh nghiệp), rơi vào tình thế
wind up.contextSentence: If the firm fails to secure bridge financing, creditors will force the directors to wind up the business.

bottle up.definition: Repress or conceal one’s feelings, emotions, or grievances over a prolonged period.
bottle up.vietnamese: kìm nén cảm xúc, giữ kín nỗi uất ức trong lòng
bottle up.contextSentence: Bottling up workplace grievances invariably leads to explosive burnout or sudden resignations.

summon up.definition: Manage to call forth, gather, or produce energy, courage, or a mental image from within oneself.
summon up.vietnamese: lấy hết can đảm, khơi dậy nguồn năng lượng/ký ức từ bên trong
summon up.contextSentence: She had to summon up all her moral fortitude to whistleblow against the fraudulent billing scheme.

chalk up.definition: Ascribe or attribute a success or failure to a particular cause or factor; register an achievement.
chalk up.vietnamese: ghi nhận chiến tích, quy nguyên nhân cho điều gì
chalk up.contextSentence: Let’s chalk up the botched presentation to jet lag and inadequate rehearsals rather than incompetence.

cheer up.definition: Become or cause someone to become less unhappy and more confident or animated.
cheer up.vietnamese: phấn chấn lên, làm ai vui vẻ trở lại
cheer up.contextSentence: Colleagues organized a surprise lunch to cheer up the lead developer after the delayed launch.

whip up.definition: Deliberately excite or stimulate intense emotions or support, often recklessly; or prepare something quickly.
whip up.vietnamese: kích động (dư luận/cảm xúc), chuẩn bị vội vàng
whip up.contextSentence: Populist tabloids regularly whip up public hysteria over speculative immigration statistics.

burn up.definition: Be destroyed completely by heat or fire; or consume energy rapidly.
burn up.vietnamese: thiêu rụi hoàn toàn, đốt sạch năng lượng
burn up.contextSentence: Spacecraft must enter the upper atmosphere at a precise angle, lest they burn up from thermal friction.

figure out.definition: Discover, solve, or understand something through thought, calculation, or investigation.
figure out.vietnamese: tìm ra lời giải, thấu suốt vấn đề qua suy nghĩ
figure out.contextSentence: It took the cryptanalysts six sleepless weeks to figure out the key exchange vulnerability.

phase out.definition: Gradually stop using, providing, or producing something over a scheduled timetable.
phase out.vietnamese: loại bỏ từng bước theo lộ trình định sẵn
phase out.contextSentence: The automotive alliance committed to phase out internal combustion drivetrains by 2035.

burn out.definition: Ruin one’s health or energy through severe, prolonged overwork; fail through overheating.
burn out.vietnamese: kiệt sức, cháy sạch sinh lực vì làm việc quá độ
burn out.contextSentence: Junior doctors frequently burn out during grueling eighty-hour residency rotations.

single out.definition: Choose one person or thing from a group for special treatment, praise, or criticism.
single out.vietnamese: chọn riêng ra để biểu dương hoặc chỉ trích đích danh
single out.contextSentence: It is unfair to single out one junior engineer for an outage caused by systemic pipeline bugs.

hammer out.definition: Negotiate or reach an agreement, resolution, or compromise through hard discussion and persistent effort.
hammer out.vietnamese: thương thảo đạt thỏa thuận sau nhiều tranh luận căng thẳng
hammer out.contextSentence: Negotiators worked through the weekend to hammer out the bilateral free-trade treaty.

flesh out.definition: Add more details, substance, or evidence to an idea, skeleton plan, or argument.
flesh out.vietnamese: bổ sung chi tiết, bồi đắp da thịt cho một ý tưởng sơ khởi
flesh out.contextSentence: The pitch deck establishes a compelling thesis, but the founders must flesh out their unit economics.

rule out.definition: Exclude something from consideration or eliminate as a possibility.
rule out.vietnamese: loại trừ, bác bỏ khả năng
rule out.contextSentence: Detectives have ruled out arson after finding proof of an electrical conduit arc.

iron out.definition: Resolve or settle minor problems, discrepancies, or difficulties.
iron out.vietnamese: giải quyết các khúc mắc nhỏ, ủi phẳng bất đồng tồn đọng
iron out.contextSentence: The two legal teams met to iron out minor indemnification clauses before signing.

crack down.definition: Take severe measures against individuals or behaviors that violate laws or rules.
crack down.vietnamese: trấn áp, siết chặt kỷ cương, xử lý mạnh tay
crack down.contextSentence: The aviation authority decided to crack down on unauthorized drone operations near runways.

pare down.definition: Reduce something in size, amount, or scope by gradually cutting away superfluous elements.
pare down.vietnamese: cắt giảm tinh gọn, lược bỏ phần thừa
pare down.contextSentence: To survive the funding winter, leadership had to pare down operating expenses by thirty percent.

boil down.definition: Reduce a complex situation, argument, or text to its most fundamental elements.
boil down.vietnamese: quy lại thành, rút cục chỉ còn là bản chất cốt lõi
boil down.contextSentence: The entire five-day symposium boils down to a single question: who controls AI governance?

nail down.definition: Finalize, confirm, or define terms precisely and conclusively.
nail down.vietnamese: chốt hạ dứt điểm, cố định chi tiết không cho thay đổi
nail down.contextSentence: We must nail down the delivery milestones before submitting the formal RFP response.

cool down.definition: Become less hot; or become calmer after high excitement, tension, or rage.
cool down.vietnamese: hạ nhiệt, bình tĩnh trở lại sau cơn giận
cool down.contextSentence: The mediator called a recess to allow both agitated factions to cool down.

narrow down.definition: Reduce the number of possibilities or choices by filtering out unsuitable ones.
narrow down.vietnamese: thu hẹp danh sách lựa chọn/phạm vi
narrow down.contextSentence: The search committee managed to narrow down two hundred applicants to three finalists.

play down.definition: Make something seem less important, serious, or consequential than it really is.
play down.vietnamese: nói giảm nói tránh, tìm cách hạ thấp mức độ nghiêm trọng
play down.contextSentence: Corporate spokespeople attempted to play down the severity of the user data leak.

tone down.definition: Make a speech, piece of writing, or opinion less harsh, extreme, or offensive.
tone down.vietnamese: làm dịu giọng, tiết chế lời lẽ bớt gay gắt
tone down.contextSentence: The legal team advised the marketing head to tone down aggressive advertising claims about rivals.

call off.definition: Cancel an event, arrangement, or planned course of action.
call off.vietnamese: hủy bỏ sự kiện, đình chỉ kế hoạch
call off.contextSentence: Torrential monsoons forced event organizers to call off the marathon.

ward off.definition: Prevent someone or something from harming you or causing difficulty; avert.
ward off.vietnamese: ngăn ngừa, phòng ngừa mối nguy hại, đẩy lui rủi ro
ward off.contextSentence: Regular cardiovascular exercise and balanced sleep help ward off metabolic degeneration.

shrug off.definition: Dismiss something as unimportant or treat an insult, injury, or setback with indifferent unconcern.
shrug off.vietnamese: phủi tay coi như không, gạt bỏ lo lắng/lời chỉ trích
shrug off.contextSentence: Veteran executives learn to shrug off sensationalist blog criticisms and focus on fundamentals.

pay off.definition: Yield good results, succeed; or settle a debt or balance completely.
pay off.vietnamese: đem lại thành quả xứng đáng, trả dứt điểm nợ nần
pay off.contextSentence: Ten years of disciplined deliberate practice finally paid off when she won the international concerto gold.

set off.definition: Begin a journey; or cause a series of events, an alarm, or an explosion to trigger.
set off.vietnamese: khởi hành, kích hoạt chuỗi phản ứng/chuông báo
set off.contextSentence: A sudden spike in consumer defaults set off panic throughout regional banking desks.

stave off.definition: Avert or delay something dangerous, difficult, or unwelcome temporarily.
stave off.vietnamese: tạm thời đẩy lui, ngăn chặn được mối nguy trong gang tấc
stave off.contextSentence: Emergency central bank liquidity injections staved off an immediate run on mutual funds.

write off.definition: Dismiss someone or something as a failure or loss; cancel a bad debt from accounting books.
write off.vietnamese: xóa nợ xấu, xem như đã mất trắng hoặc hoàn toàn thất bại
write off.contextSentence: Financial analysts cautioned that it was premature to write off the electric vehicle startup.

peel off.definition: Separate from a main group or trajectory; or remove a layer smoothly.
peel off.vietnamese: tách lẻ khỏi đội hình, bóc tách ra
peel off.contextSentence: During the high-speed flight demonstration, the wingman peeled off to initiate a solo climbing roll.

bank on.definition: Rely with confidence on someone or something happening; stake plans on an assumption.
bank on.vietnamese: trông cậy vào, đặt cược niềm tin vào điều gì
bank on.contextSentence: The founders banked on rapid organic word-of-mouth rather than investing in paid acquisition.

latch on.definition: Attach oneself firmly to something; comprehend an idea quickly; adopt an interest avidly.
latch on.vietnamese: bám chặt lấy cơ hội, nhanh chóng nắm bắt ý tưởng
latch on.contextSentence: Venture funds quickly latched on to generative synthetic media, pouring billions into pre-revenue startups.

spur on.definition: Encourage someone to continue or to make greater efforts; stimulate progress.
spur on.vietnamese: thúc đẩy, khích lệ ai tiến lên phía trước
spur on.contextSentence: Fierce competition from open-source alternatives spurred on the proprietary labs to accelerate releases.

bring on.definition: Cause something, typically unpleasant or challenging, to happen or develop; or introduce.
bring on.vietnamese: gây ra (bệnh tật, khủng hoảng), đem lại hậu quả xấu
bring on.contextSentence: Chronic sleep deprivation can bring on cognitive fog and severe cardiovascular stress.

dwell on.definition: Think, speak, or write about something, especially an unhappy or stressful subject, at excessive length.
dwell on.vietnamese: day dứt mãi, chìm đắm suy nghĩ tiêu cực về quá khứ
dwell on.contextSentence: Productive leaders dissect failed experiments dispassionately without dwelling on personal remorse.

frown on.definition: Disapprove of something morally, culturally, or professionally.
frown on.vietnamese: không tán thành, cau mày bất bình trước hành vi nào đó
frown on.contextSentence: Peer-reviewed academic communities frown on undisclosed use of generative text in grant applications.

embark on.definition: Start, begin, or initiate a course of action, project, or journey.
embark on.vietnamese: bắt tay thực hiện, dấn thân vào một hành trình lớn
embark on.contextSentence: The engineering team is about to embark on a multi-year migration to microservices.

press on.definition: Continue moving forward or making progress, especially in a determined manner despite difficulties.
press on.vietnamese: kiên cường tiến bước, tiếp tục bền bỉ vượt gian khó
press on.contextSentence: Despite debilitating headwinds and freezing sleet, the expedition pressed on toward the mountain ridge.

gloss over.definition: Treat a problem, fault, or embarrassing fact briefly or superficially so as to avoid drawing attention to it.
gloss over.vietnamese: lướt qua, cố tình bỏ qua hoặc che đậy chi tiết khó chịu
gloss over.contextSentence: The official history of the school glosses over the decades when it refused to admit girls.

paper over.definition: Hide a problem or disagreement temporarily without actually resolving it.
paper over.vietnamese: che đậy tạm thời, xoa dịu bề ngoài mà không giải quyết tận gốc
paper over.contextSentence: The coalition partners papered over their differences on immigration just long enough to win the election.

mull over.definition: Think about something carefully and at length before reaching a decision.
mull over.vietnamese: nghiền ngẫm, cân nhắc kỹ lưỡng trước khi quyết định
mull over.contextSentence: She spent the weekend mulling over the job offer from a university on the other side of the country.

win over.definition: Persuade someone to support or agree with you, especially after initial opposition or doubt.
win over.vietnamese: thuyết phục được, lôi kéo ai về phía mình
win over.contextSentence: The young chef's simple, honest cooking won over even the town's most conservative diners.

follow through.definition: Continue an action or plan until it is completed; carry out a promise or threat.
follow through.vietnamese: thực hiện đến nơi đến chốn, theo đuổi tới cùng
follow through.contextSentence: The government announced ambitious plans for rural clinics but never followed through with the funding.

muddle through.definition: Manage to cope or succeed despite lacking proper planning, skill, or resources.
muddle through.vietnamese: xoay xở cho qua, lóng ngóng nhưng rồi cũng vượt qua được
muddle through.contextSentence: With no instructions and a toddler underfoot, we somehow muddled through assembling the bookcase.

scrape through.definition: Succeed in passing an exam or getting through a difficult situation by a very narrow margin.
scrape through.vietnamese: đỗ sát nút, vượt qua một cách chật vật
scrape through.contextSentence: He barely revised for his chemistry finals and only scraped through with the minimum pass mark.

see through.definition: Recognize the true nature of someone or something and not be deceived by it.
see through.vietnamese: nhìn thấu, nhận ra bản chất thật (không bị lừa)
see through.contextSentence: Voters quickly saw through the candidate's promise to cut taxes and raise spending at the same time.

claw back.definition: Regain something lost, such as money, ground, or support, gradually and with great effort; or recover money already paid out.
claw back.vietnamese: giành lại từng chút một một cách chật vật; thu hồi khoản tiền đã chi trả
claw back.contextSentence: After a disastrous first half, the visiting team clawed back two goals in the final ten minutes.

fall back on.definition: Turn to something or someone for support when other options have failed.
fall back on.vietnamese: dựa vào, cầu viện đến (phương án dự phòng)
fall back on.contextSentence: When the harvest failed, families fell back on their savings and the vegetables in their home gardens.

cut back.definition: Reduce the amount of something, especially spending or consumption.
cut back.vietnamese: cắt giảm (chi tiêu, mức tiêu thụ)
cut back.contextSentence: Her doctor advised her to cut back on salt and coffee after the blood pressure check.

fritter away.definition: Waste time, money, or energy gradually on trivial things.
fritter away.vietnamese: phung phí dần dần, tiêu xài hoang phí vào những thứ vụn vặt
fritter away.contextSentence: He frittered away his inheritance on gadgets and holidays and had nothing left by thirty.

chip away at.definition: Gradually reduce or weaken something through persistent small efforts.
chip away at.vietnamese: bào mòn dần, từng bước làm suy yếu hoặc giảm bớt
chip away at.contextSentence: She chipped away at her student debt by tutoring every weekend for three years.

whittle away.definition: Gradually reduce the size, amount, or strength of something through repeated small reductions.
whittle away.vietnamese: gọt dần, làm hao mòn từng chút một
whittle away.contextSentence: Successive amendments whittled away the protections that the original law had given to tenants.

cave in.definition: Collapse inward; figuratively, give in to pressure or demands after a period of resistance.
cave in.vietnamese: sụp đổ; (nghĩa bóng) nhượng bộ, đầu hàng trước sức ép
cave in.contextSentence: After three weeks of strikes, management caved in and agreed to restore the night-shift bonus.

factor in.definition: Include something as a relevant element when making a calculation, plan, or decision.
factor in.vietnamese: tính đến, đưa vào cân nhắc hoặc tính toán
factor in.contextSentence: When you budget for the trip, remember to factor in airport transfers and visa fees.

rein in.definition: Restrict or bring under control something that is excessive or unruly.
rein in.vietnamese: kiềm chế, kìm hãm, siết lại trong tầm kiểm soát
rein in.contextSentence: The new governor promised to rein in public spending without closing rural schools.

skirt around.definition: Avoid dealing with or talking directly about a difficult or awkward subject.
skirt around.vietnamese: né tránh, lảng tránh, nói vòng vo quanh vấn đề
skirt around.contextSentence: The interview skirted around the actor's legal troubles and focused instead on his new film.

come across as.definition: Give a particular impression to other people.
come across as.vietnamese: tạo ấn tượng là, có vẻ như (trong mắt người khác)
come across as.contextSentence: He doesn't mean to be rude, but his short emails can come across as cold.

get across.definition: Communicate an idea successfully so that it is understood.
get across.vietnamese: truyền đạt được, làm cho người khác hiểu
get across.contextSentence: The museum uses interactive models to get across how earthquakes actually form.

chiasmus.root: Greek khiasmos (crossing, diagonal arrangement), from khiazein (to mark with an X, chi).
chiasmus.definition: Scheme of Balance: [A - B] : [B' - A'] (Criss-cross syntactic structure without identical word repetition).
chiasmus.vietnamese: Phép đối chéo cú pháp (đối xứng chữ X); đảo trật tự ngữ pháp giữa hai vế để tạo nhịp điệu nhã nhặn và chiều sâu triết lý.
chiasmus.contextSentence: 'By day the frolic, and the dance by night.' — Samuel Johnson, The Vanity of Human Wishes.

antimetabole.definition: Scheme of Balance: [Word A ... Word B] -> [Word B ... Word A] (Strict lexical inversion across parallel clauses).
antimetabole.vietnamese: Phép điệp đảo từ vựng; lặp lại chính xác các từ nhưng đổi ngược vị trí nhằm tạo ra sự hoán đổi ý nghĩa sâu sắc và dứt khoát.
antimetabole.contextSentence: 'Ask not what your country can do for you—ask what you can do for your country.' — John F. Kennedy.

anaphora.root: Greek ana- (back, again) + pherein (to carry, bear).
anaphora.definition: Scheme of Repetition: [Anchor X ... Clause 1], [Anchor X ... Clause 2], [Anchor X ... Clause 3].
anaphora.vietnamese: Phép điệp ngữ đầu câu (thủ vĩ tương ứng); lặp từ/ngữ ở đầu các vế liên tiếp nhằm dồn nén cảm xúc và tăng cường uy lực thuyết phục.
anaphora.contextSentence: 'We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields.' — Winston Churchill.

epistrophe.root: Greek epi- (upon, in addition) + strophe (turning). Also termed Epiphora.
epistrophe.definition: Scheme of Repetition: [Clause 1 ... Anchor Y], [Clause 2 ... Anchor Y], [Clause 3 ... Anchor Y].
epistrophe.vietnamese: Phép điệp ngữ cuối câu; lặp lại từ hoặc ngữ ở cuối các mệnh đề liên tiếp để tạo âm hưởng vang vọng và khắc sâu kết luận.
epistrophe.contextSentence: '...government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.' — Abraham Lincoln.

symploce.definition: Scheme of Repetition: [Anchor X ... Anchor Y], [Anchor X ... Anchor Y] (Combination of Anaphora + Epistrophe).
symploce.vietnamese: Phép song điệp thủ vĩ; kết hợp điệp đầu và điệp đuôi đồng thời, tạo nên cấu trúc lồng ghép đóng khung mệnh đề cực kỳ chặt chẽ.
symploce.contextSentence: 'When there is talk of hatred, let us stand up and talk against it. When there is talk of violence, let us stand up and talk against it.' — Bill Clinton.

anadiplosis.definition: Scheme of Repetition: [Clause 1 ... Word A] -> [Word A ... Clause 2] (End of clause repeats at start of next).
anadiplosis.vietnamese: Phép điệp liên hoàn (điệp đầu nối đuôi); từ cuối câu trước trở thành từ mở đầu câu sau, tạo chuỗi nhân quả mắt xích không thể tách rời.
anadiplosis.contextSentence: 'Fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. Hate leads to suffering.' — Yoda / George Lucas.

epanalepsis.root: Greek epi- (in addition) + ana- (again) + lambanein (to take).
epanalepsis.definition: Scheme of Repetition: [Anchor X ... intervening text ... Anchor X] (Beginning repeated at end).
epanalepsis.vietnamese: Phép điệp vòng tròn; từ mở đầu câu được lặp lại ở chính cuối câu đó, tạo ấn tượng tuần hoàn khép kín hoặc chân lý tất yếu.
epanalepsis.contextSentence: 'Blood hath bought blood, and blows have answer'd blows.' — William Shakespeare, King John.

polysyndeton.root: Greek poly- (many) + syndetos (bound together with conjunctions).
polysyndeton.definition: Scheme of Addition: [Item 1] AND [Item 2] AND [Item 3] AND [Item 4] (Deliberate abundance of conjunctions).
polysyndeton.vietnamese: Phép liên từ trùng điệp; cố tình lặp lại liên từ nối nhiều lần nhằm tạo cảm giác dồn dập, tích tụ sức nặng và quy mô to lớn.
polysyndeton.contextSentence: 'And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house...' — Matthew 7:27.

asyndeton.definition: Scheme of Omission: [Item 1], [Item 2], [Item 3], [Item 4] (Omission of coordinating conjunctions).
asyndeton.vietnamese: Phép tỉnh lược liên từ; lược bỏ hoàn toàn các liên từ nối giữa các vế câu nhằm tạo nhịp văn dồn dập, gãy gọn, dứt khoát.
asyndeton.contextSentence: 'Veni, vidi, vici. (I came, I saw, I conquered.)' — Julius Caesar.

zeugma.definition: Scheme of Wordplay: [Verb V] governs both [Concrete Noun A] and [Abstract Noun B] with dual senses.
zeugma.vietnamese: Phép ách ngữ (dùng một động/tính từ chi phối hai danh từ với hai sắc thái nghĩa đen và nghĩa bóng khác nhau); tạo bất ngờ và ý vị sâu cay.
zeugma.contextSentence: 'She arrived in a taxi and a state of utter distress.' — P.G. Wodehouse.

syllepsis.root: Greek syn- (together) + lambanein (to take). Closely related to Zeugma.
syllepsis.definition: Scheme of Wordplay: [Verb V] is grammatically or semantically incongruous with one of two governed objects.
syllepsis.vietnamese: Phép đồng chấp ngữ nghĩa; một từ đơn lẻ kết nối hai thực thể một cách bất cân xứng giữa vật lý cụ thể và tâm lý trừu tượng.
syllepsis.contextSentence: 'He carried a strobe light and the responsibility for the lives of his men.' — Tim O'Brien, The Things They Carried.

litotes.definition: Trope of Understatement: Denying the contrary: NOT + [Negative Adj/Adv] = Emphatic Positive.
litotes.vietnamese: Phép nói giảm qua phủ định hai lần; dùng sự phủ định của điều tiêu cực để khẳng định mạnh mẽ một sự thật tích cực, giữ thái độ khiêm nhường.
litotes.contextSentence: 'A citizen of no mean city.' — Acts 21:39 (St. Paul meaning a very famous city).

hypophora.root: Greek hypo- (under) + pherein (to carry, put forward).
hypophora.definition: Discursive Strategy: [Question Q posed by speaker] -> [Immediate direct Answer A supplied by speaker].
hypophora.vietnamese: Phép tự vấn tự đáp; diễn giả tự đặt câu hỏi rồi lập tức tự trả lời nhằm dẫn dắt luồng tư duy của thính giả theo quỹ đạo định sẵn.
hypophora.contextSentence: 'What is our aim? I can answer in one word: It is victory, victory at all costs.' — Winston Churchill.

procatalepsis.root: Greek pro- (before) + katalambanein (to seize upon, anticipate). Also termed Prolepsis.
procatalepsis.definition: Discursive Strategy: [Anticipate opponent's counterargument] -> [Preemptively refute and neutralize it].
procatalepsis.vietnamese: Phép đón đầu phản bác; lường trước luận điểm công kích của đối phương và bẻ gãy nó ngay trong phần trình bày của mình.
procatalepsis.contextSentence: 'Now, someone will say: 'Yes, but what about the cost?' To that objection I reply...' — Cicero.

antithesis.definition: Scheme of Balance: [Idea A in Structure X] opposed to [Idea B in parallel Structure X'].
antithesis.vietnamese: Phép tương phản đối lập; đặt hai khái niệm trái ngược nhau trong hai vế câu có cấu trúc ngữ pháp song song để làm nổi bật sự thật.
antithesis.contextSentence: 'To err is human; to forgive, divine.' — Alexander Pope, An Essay on Criticism.

oxymoron.root: Greek oxys (sharp) + moros (foolish, dull) -> literally 'pointedly foolish'.
oxymoron.definition: Trope of Meaning: [Adjective contradictory to Noun] juxtaposed into a single semantic unit.
oxymoron.vietnamese: Phép nghịch hợp; ghép hai từ ngữ có ý nghĩa đối lập chan chát cạnh nhau để tạo một nghĩa mới đầy nghịch lý thâm thúy.
oxymoron.contextSentence: 'O brawling love! O loving hate! ... O heavy lightness! serious vanity!' — William Shakespeare, Romeo and Juliet.

paradox.definition: Trope of Meaning: [Proposition that appears self-contradictory yet expresses a profound truth].
paradox.vietnamese: Phép nghịch biện; mệnh đề thoạt nghe có vẻ vô lý hoặc phản trực giác nhưng khi suy ngẫm lại bộc lộ một quy luật chân lý sâu xa.
paradox.contextSentence: 'The swiftest traveler is he that goes afoot.' — Henry David Thoreau, Walden.

hyperbaton.definition: Scheme of Word Order: Inversion or displacement of conventional syntactic word order for dramatic emphasis.
hyperbaton.vietnamese: Phép đảo loạn cú pháp; cố tình xáo trộn trật tự thông thường của từ ngữ trong câu nhằm tạo điểm nhấn kịch tính và thu hút chú ý.
hyperbaton.contextSentence: 'Some rise by sin, and some by virtue fall.' — William Shakespeare, Measure for Measure.

anastrophe.root: Greek ana- (back, upside down) + strephein (to turn).
anastrophe.definition: Scheme of Word Order: Inversion of natural word order, particularly placing an adjective after its noun or verb before subject.
anastrophe.vietnamese: Phép đảo ngược từ loại; đảo danh-tính từ hoặc động-chủ từ để tạo ngữ điệu trang nghiêm, thi vị hoặc cổ kính.
anastrophe.contextSentence: 'Deep into that darkness peering, long I stood there wondering, fearing...' — Edgar Allan Poe, The Raven.

parenthesis.definition: Scheme of Insertion: [Main Clause Start ... (Extraneous qualifying information) ... Main Clause End].
parenthesis.vietnamese: Phép chêm xen cú pháp; chèn một cụm từ hoặc mệnh đề phụ giải thích vào giữa một câu hoàn chỉnh mà không làm hỏng cấu trúc chính.
parenthesis.contextSentence: 'And what is so rare as a day in June? / Then, if ever, come perfect days.' — James Russell Lowell.

apposition.definition: Scheme of Insertion: [Noun Phrase 1], [Noun Phrase 2 adjacent clarifying or renaming 1].
apposition.vietnamese: Phép đồng vị ngữ; đặt hai danh từ/cụm danh từ liền kề nhau để một bên bổ nghĩa và xác định bản chất cho bên kia.
apposition.contextSentence: 'John of Gaunt, time-honored Lancaster.' — William Shakespeare, Richard II.

ellipsis.root: Greek elleipein (to leave out, fall short).
ellipsis.definition: Scheme of Omission: [Subject/Verb omitted in second clause because clearly understood from first].
ellipsis.vietnamese: Phép tỉnh lược ngữ pháp; lược bỏ từ ngữ đã xuất hiện ở vế trước nhằm tránh lặp thừa và tăng tính hàm súc cô đọng.
ellipsis.contextSentence: 'To err is human; to forgive, divine.' (Omission of 'is' in second clause).

aposiopesis.root: Greek apo- (away) + siopan (to be silent) -> 'becoming silent'.
aposiopesis.definition: Scheme of Omission: [Sentence breaks off abruptly before completion, leaving thought unsaid].
aposiopesis.vietnamese: Phép đứt mạch ngôn từ; đột ngột ngừng câu giữa chừng khi cảm xúc lên đến đỉnh điểm hoặc ngụ ý những điều không thể nói hết.
aposiopesis.contextSentence: 'She looked at the contract, realized the trap, and then... but words fail to describe the betrayal.'

paralipsis.root: Greek para- (beside) + leipein (to leave). Also known as Apophasis or Praeteritio.
paralipsis.definition: Trope of Irony: [Stating that one will not mention topic X, thereby drawing maximum attention to X].
paralipsis.vietnamese: Phép nói tránh giả vờ; tuyên bố sẽ không đề cập đến một sự việc nhưng qua đó lại nhấn mạnh và phơi bày chính sự việc đó.
paralipsis.contextSentence: 'I will not speak of his embezzlements, his deceit, nor his failed past ventures.' — Classical oratory.

epizeuxis.root: Greek epi- (upon) + zeugnunai (to yoke, join together).
epizeuxis.definition: Scheme of Repetition: [Word A], [Word A], [Word A] (Immediate contiguous repetition with zero intervening words).
epizeuxis.vietnamese: Phép điệp từ liền kề; lặp lại một từ nhiều lần liên tiếp không có từ chen giữa nhằm nhấn mạnh tột cùng tính khẩn cấp hoặc ám ảnh.

diacope.root: Greek dia- (through) + koptein (to cut) -> 'cutting in two'.
diacope.definition: Scheme of Repetition: [Word A] ... [intervening word(s)] ... [Word A] (Repetition broken by brief insert).
diacope.vietnamese: Phép điệp từ xen kẽ; lặp lại từ hoặc cụm từ được ngăn cách bởi một hoặc vài từ ngắn ở giữa nhằm tạo nhịp đập cảm xúc mãnh liệt.
diacope.contextSentence: 'Bond. James Bond.' / 'A horse! a horse! my kingdom for a horse!' — William Shakespeare, Richard III.

polyptoton.definition: Scheme of Repetition: Repetition of words derived from the same morphological root in different grammatical forms.
polyptoton.vietnamese: Phép điệp gốc từ (đồng nguyên tự); lặp lại các biến thể từ vựng cùng chung một gốc hình thái trong cùng một câu.
polyptoton.contextSentence: 'With eager feeding food doth choke the feeder.' — William Shakespeare, Richard II.

antanaclasis.root: Greek anti- (against) + anaklan (to bend back, reflect).
antanaclasis.definition: Scheme of Wordplay: Repeating a single word within a sentence, but shifting its meaning on the repetition.
antanaclasis.vietnamese: Phép biến nghĩa điệp từ; lặp lại cùng một từ ngữ nhưng mỗi lần xuất hiện lại mang một nét nghĩa hoàn toàn khác nhau.
antanaclasis.contextSentence: 'If we do not hang together, we shall most assuredly hang separately.' — Benjamin Franklin.

paronomasia.root: Greek para- (beside) + onomazein (to name) -> 'play on words'.
paronomasia.definition: Scheme of Wordplay: A rhetorical pun exploiting words with similar sounds but completely different definitions.
paronomasia.vietnamese: Phép chơi chữ đồng âm/gần âm; khai thác sự tương đồng về ngữ âm giữa các từ có nghĩa khác biệt để tạo sự dí dỏm sâu cay.
paronomasia.contextSentence: 'A little more than kin, and less than kind.' — William Shakespeare, Hamlet.

metaphor.definition: Trope of Comparison: [Target Concept A] IS directly stated as [Source Vehicle B] without 'like' or 'as'.
metaphor.vietnamese: Phép ẩn dụ; chuyển đổi trường nghĩa từ đối tượng này sang đối tượng khác một cách trực tiếp không dùng từ so sánh, kích thích liên tưởng.
metaphor.contextSentence: 'All the world's a stage, and all the men and women merely players.' — William Shakespeare.

simile.definition: Trope of Comparison: [Target Concept A] is compared to [Source Concept B] using explicit markers 'like' or 'as'.
simile.vietnamese: Phép so sánh tu từ; đối chiếu hai đối tượng khác loại qua các từ so sánh như 'như', 'tựa như' để làm sáng tỏ phẩm chất.
simile.contextSentence: 'O my Luve is like a red, red rose / That's newly sprung in June.' — Robert Burns.

metonymy.definition: Trope of Substitution: Substituting the name of an attribute or closely associated adjunct for that of the thing meant.
metonymy.vietnamese: Phép hoán dụ cận kề; dùng một dấu hiệu, thuộc tính hoặc vật gắn liền mật thiết để đại diện cho toàn bộ đối tượng.
metonymy.contextSentence: 'The pen is mightier than the sword.' — Edward Bulwer-Lytton (pen = discourse; sword = military force).

synecdoche.root: Greek syn- (together) + ekdekhesthai (to understand, take up).
synecdoche.definition: Trope of Substitution: A part is used to represent the whole, or the whole is used to represent a part.
synecdoche.vietnamese: Phép hoán dụ bộ phận; dùng một phần cụ thể để chỉ toàn thể hoặc ngược lại nhằm tạo hình ảnh trực quan sinh động.
synecdoche.contextSentence: 'All hands on deck.' (hands = sailors / entire individuals).

catachresis.root: Greek kata- (down, against) + khresthai (to use) -> 'misuse, strained metaphor'.
catachresis.definition: Trope of Meaning: A highly paradoxical, strained, or mixed metaphor deliberately used for arresting cognitive effect.
catachresis.vietnamese: Phép ẩn dụ nghịch dị (dùng từ trái khoáy); kết hợp hình ảnh mâu thuẫn kỳ lạ nhằm gây ấn tượng thị giác và kích hoạt tư duy người nghe.
catachresis.contextSentence: 'To take arms against a sea of troubles...' — William Shakespeare, Hamlet.

personification.root: Latin persona (mask, person) + facere (to make). Also termed Prosopopoeia.
personification.definition: Trope of Meaning: Attributing human qualities, volition, or emotional agency to non-human entities or abstract concepts.
personification.vietnamese: Phép nhân hóa; gán ghép hành vi, tâm tư tình cảm của con người cho sự vật vô tri, máy móc hoặc khái niệm trừu tượng.
personification.contextSentence: 'Time and tide wait for no man.' — Proverb.

anthropomorphism.definition: Trope of Meaning: Treating non-human animals, deities, or objects as literally having human physical form and motivations.
anthropomorphism.vietnamese: Phép nhân hình hóa; miêu tả sự vật hoặc sinh vật như thể chúng thực sự có nhân hình và động cơ tâm lý như con người.
anthropomorphism.contextSentence: 'The engine groaned, coughed in protest, and stubbornly refused to ignite.'

hyperbole.definition: Trope of Exaggeration: Exaggerated statements or claims not meant to be taken literally, used for rhetorical emphasis.
hyperbole.vietnamese: Phép ngoa dụ (nói quá); phóng đại tính chất, quy mô của sự vật hiện tượng nhằm khắc sâu ấn tượng và gia tăng sức truyền cảm.
hyperbole.contextSentence: 'I loved Ophelia: forty thousand brothers could not, with all their quantity of love, make up my sum.' — William Shakespeare.

meiosis.definition: Trope of Understatement: Belittling or downplaying the gravity, scale, or significance of an enormous event.
meiosis.vietnamese: Phép nói giảm mức độ; miêu tả một đại họa hoặc sự kiện kinh hoàng bằng ngôn từ nhẹ nhàng tối giản để tạo hiệu ứng mỉa mai.
meiosis.contextSentence: 'It's just a flesh wound.' — Monty Python and the Holy Grail (referring to a severed arm).

euphemism.definition: Trope of Softening: A mild or indirect word or expression substituted for one considered harsh, blunt, or offensive.
euphemism.vietnamese: Phép uyển ngữ (nói khéo); dùng từ ngữ nhẹ nhàng, gián tiếp để tránh gây đau buồn, xúc phạm hoặc né tránh cảm giác thô lỗ.
euphemism.contextSentence: 'Passed away' instead of 'died'; 'letting employees go' instead of 'firing'.

dysphemism.definition: Trope of Pejorative: A derogatory or unpleasant term used instead of a pleasant or neutral one; reverse of euphemism.
dysphemism.vietnamese: Phép miệt thị ngữ; cố tình dùng từ ngữ thô ráp, tiêu cực thay cho từ trung tính để châm biếm, phê phán hoặc biểu thị khinh miệt.
dysphemism.contextSentence: 'Snail mail' for physical postal delivery; 'grease monkey' for auto mechanic.

irony.definition: Trope of Contrast: Expression of meaning by using language that signifies the opposite, typically for humor or emphasis.
irony.vietnamese: Phép nghịch mỉa (mỉa mai tình huống/ngữ nghĩa); dùng lời lẽ biểu đạt trái ngược với bản chất thực tế nhằm làm nổi bật mâu thuẫn trớ trêu.
irony.contextSentence: 'Water, water, everywhere, / Nor any drop to drink.' — S.T. Coleridge, The Rime of the Ancient Mariner.

sarcasm.root: Greek sarkazein (to tear flesh, bite the lips in rage).
sarcasm.definition: Trope of Mockery: The use of irony to mock, convey contempt, or wound an opponent directly.
sarcasm.vietnamese: Phép châm biếm đả kích; hình thức mỉa mai gay gắt có chủ đích làm tổn thương, bộc lộ sự khinh khi hoặc phản bác không khoan nhượng.
sarcasm.contextSentence: 'Oh, a brilliant strategy indeed—let us bankrupt our operating reserves on untested promotional billboards!'

apostrophe.definition: Discursive Strategy: Speaker turns aside from the direct audience to address an absent person, deity, or abstract idea.
apostrophe.vietnamese: Phép hô ngữ cảm thán; diễn giả bất ngờ quay sang kêu gọi, trò chuyện trực tiếp với một người vắng mặt hoặc một khái niệm trừu tượng.
apostrophe.contextSentence: 'O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?' — 1 Corinthians 15:55.

erotema.root: Greek erotan (to ask a question). Rhetorical Question.
erotema.definition: Discursive Strategy: A question asked for effect or to lay down a presupposition, without expectation of a reply.
erotema.vietnamese: Phép câu hỏi tu từ; đặt câu hỏi không nhằm tìm kiếm câu trả lời mà để khẳng định một chân lý hiển nhiên không thể bác bỏ.
erotema.contextSentence: 'If you prick us, do we not bleed? If you tickle us, do we not laugh?' — William Shakespeare, The Merchant of Venice.

pleonasm.definition: Scheme of Redundancy: The use of more words than are necessary to convey meaning, for stylistic emphasis or vividness.
pleonasm.vietnamese: Phép thừa từ tu từ; dùng nhiều từ hơn mức cần thiết về mặt logic ngữ nghĩa nhằm khắc họa sống động hoặc nhấn mạnh triệt để.
pleonasm.contextSentence: 'I saw it with my own eyes.' / 'Black darkness enveloped the terrain.'

tautology.definition: Scheme of Redundancy: The unnecessary repetition of an idea, statement, or word in immediately synonymous terms.
tautology.vietnamese: Phép trùng ngôn tu từ; lặp lại cùng một ý tưởng bằng các từ đồng nghĩa liền kề, tạo hiệu ứng dứt khoát hoặc nhịp điệu dân gian.
tautology.contextSentence: 'A free gift' / 'Adequate enough' / 'They arrived one after another in succession.'

periphrasis.definition: Trope of Circumlocution: Use of an indirect, roundabout, or multi-word expression in place of a single concise word.
periphrasis.vietnamese: Phép nói vòng (uyển khúc ngữ); dùng cụm từ miêu tả đặc trưng thay vì gọi trực tiếp tên sự vật để tạo vẻ trang trọng hoặc gợi cảm.
periphrasis.contextSentence: 'The elongated yellow fruit' for banana; 'the city that never sleeps' for New York.

kenning.root: Old Norse kenna (to know, perceive, name).
kenning.definition: Trope of Poetic Compound: A figurative, multi-part metaphor used in Old English and Norse poetry in place of a simple noun.
kenning.vietnamese: Phép định danh thi ca; dùng cụm từ ghép hình tượng cổ để thay thế cho một danh từ phổ thông, tạo phong vị sử thi tráng lệ.
kenning.contextSentence: 'Whale-road' for the sea; 'sky-candle' for the sun; 'battle-sweat' for blood.

onomatopoeia.definition: Phonaesthetic Figure: The formation of a word from a sound associated with what is named.
onomatopoeia.vietnamese: Phép từ tượng thanh; sáng tạo từ ngữ mô phỏng trực tiếp âm thanh tự nhiên của đối tượng nhằm khơi dậy thính giác người đọc.
onomatopoeia.contextSentence: 'The moan of doves in immemorial elms, / And murmuring of innumerable bees.' — Alfred, Lord Tennyson.

alliteration.definition: Phonaesthetic Figure: Repetition of the same initial consonant sound in successive or closely associated words.
alliteration.vietnamese: Phép điệp phụ âm đầu; lặp lại âm đầu của các từ liên tiếp nhằm tạo nhạc tính, nhịp điệu hài hòa và sự dễ nhớ cho câu khẩu hiệu.
alliteration.contextSentence: 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.' / 'Doom, despair, and devastation.'

assonance.definition: Phonaesthetic Figure: Repetition of identical or similar vowel sounds in nearby words with different consonants.
assonance.vietnamese: Phép điệp nguyên âm; lặp lại nguyên âm trong các âm tiết liền kề để tạo âm hưởng êm dịu, ngân vang và tăng tính biểu cảm.
assonance.contextSentence: 'Hear the mellow wedding bells...' — Edgar Allan Poe, The Bells.

consonance.definition: Phonaesthetic Figure: Repetition of identical consonant sounds in nearby words, especially at the end of syllables.
consonance.vietnamese: Phép điệp phụ âm cuối/thân; lặp lại phụ âm ở giữa hoặc cuối từ để tạo cấu trúc âm thanh chắc chắn, đanh thép và chặt chẽ.
consonance.contextSentence: 'A stroke of luck' / 'The stroke of thick black ink.'

cacophony.definition: Phonaesthetic Figure: The deliberate use of harsh, discordant, guttural sounds to evoke turbulence, chaos, or disgust.
cacophony.vietnamese: Phép nghịch âm chói tai; cố tình dùng các âm thanh gắt gỏng, thô ráp để gợi lên không khí hỗn loạn, bạo lực hoặc khủng hoảng.
cacophony.contextSentence: 'Beware the Jabberwock, my son! / The jaws that bite, the claws that catch!' — Lewis Carroll.

euphony.definition: Phonaesthetic Figure: The use of words and phrases that produce a pleasing, smooth, and harmonious acoustic effect.
euphony.vietnamese: Phép thuận âm êm ái; lựa chọn từ ngữ có âm thanh nhẹ nhàng, du dương, dễ nghe để tạo cảm giác an tâm, thư thái và cao quý.
euphony.contextSentence: 'Season of mists and mellow fruitfulness, / Close bosom-friend of the maturing sun...' — John Keats, To Autumn.

climax.root: Greek klimax (ladder, staircase). Also termed Auxesis.
climax.definition: Scheme of Order: Arrangement of words, phrases, or clauses in an ascending order of importance, force, or intensity.
climax.vietnamese: Phép tiến thoái tam cấp (tiệm tiến tăng tiến); sắp xếp các vế câu theo trật tự tăng dần về mức độ quan trọng hoặc cảm xúc.
climax.contextSentence: 'I came, I saw, I conquered.' / 'Look up! Shake off the dust! Stand forth! Reign!'

anticlimax.root: Greek anti- (against) + klimax (ladder). Also termed Bathos.
anticlimax.definition: Scheme of Order: A sudden transition in discourse from an important, elevated idea to a ludicrous or trivial one.
anticlimax.vietnamese: Phép tụt dốc tu từ; bất ngờ chuyển từ không khí trang nghiêm, bi tráng sang một chi tiết tầm thường vụn vặt để gây cười hoặc châm biếm.
anticlimax.contextSentence: 'He lost his family, his fortune, his country, and his fountain pen.'

tricolon.definition: Scheme of Rhythm: A rhetorical series composed of three parallel words, phrases, or clauses of equal length.
tricolon.vietnamese: Phép tam đoạn luật (quy tắc bộ ba); kết hợp ba vế câu song song có độ dài và nhịp điệu tương đồng để tạo tính thẩm mỹ hoàn chỉnh.
tricolon.contextSentence: 'Life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.' — US Declaration of Independence.

tetracolon.definition: Scheme of Rhythm: A rhetorical series composed of four parallel words, phrases, or clauses.
tetracolon.vietnamese: Phép tứ đoạn luận; cấu trúc chuỗi bốn vế câu đối xứng nhằm tạo sự chắc chắn, vững chãi như một chiếc bàn bốn chân.
tetracolon.contextSentence: 'That government of the people, by the people, for the people, shall not perish from the earth.' (Lincoln expanded cadence).

isocolon.definition: Scheme of Rhythm: A sentence or series composed of two or more clauses of strictly equal length and grammatical structure.
isocolon.vietnamese: Phép đối cân xứng ngữ đoạn; các mệnh đề có số lượng âm tiết và cấu trúc ngữ pháp hoàn toàn bằng nhau, tạo nhịp điệu toán học.
isocolon.contextSentence: 'An envious heart makes a treacherous ear.' — Zora Neale Hurston, Their Eyes Were Watching God.

bicolon.definition: Scheme of Rhythm: A rhetorical sentence composed of two parallel clauses of equivalent cadence or syntactic shape.
bicolon.vietnamese: Phép nhị đoạn luật; kết hợp hai vế câu đối sánh ngắn gọn, xúc tích, tạo nên những câu châm ngôn ghi nhớ tức thì.
bicolon.contextSentence: 'Garbage in, garbage out.' / 'Buy low, sell high.'

hendiatris.root: Greek hen dia treis (one through three).
hendiatris.definition: Scheme of Balance: Three words expressing one single comprehensive idea (classic tripartite formula).
hendiatris.vietnamese: Phép tam ngữ quy nhất; dùng ba từ đơn độc lập liên kết lại để cùng diễn đạt trọn vẹn một ý niệm cốt lõi duy nhất.
hendiatris.contextSentence: 'Wine, women, and song.' / 'Citius, Altius, Fortius (Faster, Higher, Stronger).' — Olympic motto.

hendiadys.root: Greek hen dia dyoin (one through two).
hendiadys.definition: Scheme of Grammar: Expressing a single complex idea by joining two nouns with 'and' instead of using an adjective and a noun.
hendiadys.vietnamese: Phép nhị danh tương hợp; dùng hai danh từ nối bằng liên từ 'and' thay vì dùng tính từ bổ nghĩa cho danh từ, tạo vẻ trang nghiêm.
hendiadys.contextSentence: 'Sound and fury' (instead of furious sound); 'nice and warm' (nicely warm).

anthimeria.definition: Trope of Grammar: The substitution of one part of speech for another, most commonly using a noun as a verb.
anthimeria.vietnamese: Phép chuyển loại từ ngữ; dùng danh từ như một động từ (hoặc ngược lại) để tạo sự mới mẻ, linh hoạt và ngôn ngữ hiện đại.
anthimeria.contextSentence: 'Google it.' / 'The thunder would not peace at my bidding.' — William Shakespeare, King Lear.

enallage.definition: Scheme of Grammar: A deliberate grammatical substitution of one case, person, gender, number, or tense for another.
enallage.vietnamese: Phép sai lạc ngữ pháp có chủ ý; cố ý sử dụng sai quy tắc ngữ pháp thông thường để tạo dấu ấn thương hiệu hoặc giọng điệu tự nhiên.
enallage.contextSentence: 'We was robbed!' / 'Think different.' — Apple campaign (adverb replaced by adjective).

hypallage.root: Greek hypo- (under) + allassein (to change, exchange). Transferred Epithet.
